title: No knot overlaps: Thomsen's configuration and the 3-net of Q8
claim: (1) Doubling (the selector case of Lemma 2 of MALTSEV-CONVERSE-20261020-001B-P001): a relation whose variables Z + {t, t'} form a circuit, with Z nonempty, and which allows t' = t at every value of Z violates elimination once two copies share t and t'. (2) In a law that composes like cycles no circuit overlaps modulo the tops: elimination applied to two copies of an overlapping knot that share all but one variable yields such a relation. So every circuit's top image is a Latin hypercube of the tops, which proves the Latin conjecture of KNOT-IMAGES-20261021-001B-P001, and a law composes like cycles exactly when proper pp-definable equivalences on its ranges make every circuit functional at each variable. (3) In the 3-net law of a Latin square, Thomsen's configuration, with or without one column visible, allows every tuple with two equal rows; it is full exactly when Thomsen's closure condition holds, and otherwise one of its two forms is a knot that overlaps at every variable. So the 3-net law composes like cycles exactly when the square is isotopic to an abelian p-group; a group's 3-net law does so exactly for abelian p-groups. (4) For Q8 the configuration is the commuting-differences relation. Its top image modulo +-1, omega(c1 + c2, c1 + c3) = 0, is not preserved by x + y + z, a three-tuple replacement for the 416-equation certificate, and the system T(x1, x2, x3) & T(x1, x2, x3') violates elimination. So the 3-net law of Q8 does not compose like cycles, and Conjecture 7 of CYCLE-TOPS-20261021-001B-P001 is not refuted by it.
failure_conditions: A relation satisfying the hypothesis of (1) has a doubled system that satisfies elimination.
A law that composes like cycles has a circuit that overlaps modulo its tops.
Thomsen's configuration of a Latin square omits a tuple with two equal rows, is full while Thomsen's condition fails, or is not full while it holds.
A square violating Thomsen's condition has a doubled configuration that satisfies elimination, or a square isotopic to an abelian p-group has a 3-net law that fails elimination.
The Q8 configuration differs from the commuting-differences relation, its top image is closed under x + y + z, or the doubled system satisfies elimination.
foundation_claim_scope: Which laws compose like cycles: no overlapping circuits, Latin circuits modulo the tops, and the 3-net laws of Latin squares. No native recurrence, composed topology in the protected sense, path, metric distance or physical claim.
